name: NatWest Group plc
research_rationale: Buy screen still fits cheapness and yield; supportive conference commentary is thin versus no post-Q3 filings, so Q3 impairment, tax and rate risks keep research at accumulate, not full buy conviction.

weekly_updates.summary:
30 Oct Q3 2026 IMS: attributable profit £1.5bn, RoTE 21.6%, total income +9.6% YTD; H1 income outlook reaffirmed, RWA ~£210bn at 1 Jan 2027 (Basel 3.1).  
Q3 impairment £277m (~2× prior-year quarter) and higher YTD tax (bank surcharge) drove a share fall despite operational strength.  
Quant screen still buy (4w, stable); timing accumulate, RSI ~29.

No news or new filings since the 30 Oct Q3 IMS refresh; thesis and risks unchanged.  
Quant screen remains buy (5w, stable); timing still accumulate, RSI ~29.  
No material change.

Quant screen upgraded to Strong Buy (1w, improving); timing still accumulate, RSI ~37.  
Since 1 Nov only routine share-buyback RNS (3 Nov); press rehashes Q3 NIM/loans and possible further BoE Bank Rate rises.  
30 Oct Q3 IMS thesis unchanged—elevated impairments and surcharge/tax still temper conviction.

No new articles or filings since the 8 Nov refresh; the 30 Oct Q3 IMS thesis is unchanged.  
The quant screen is **Buy** (was Strong Buy on 8 Nov); composite ~69%, trend deteriorating; timing still **accumulate**, RSI ~37.  
No material change in impairment, surcharge/tax or BoE rate-risk narrative in supplied sources.

Since 10 Nov, press only: CFO Murray cited lending momentum, structural hedge income and cost discipline (JPMorgan, 24 Nov), and market chatter on a significant risk transfer on ~£7bn of corporate loans (23 Nov); no new RNS in the supplied batch.  
Quant screen remains **Buy** (3w, stable); timing **accumulate**, RSI ~40 (was ~37 on 10 Nov).  
30 Oct Q3 IMS narrative—elevated impairments, surcharge/tax and BoE rate overhang—is unchanged.
